posts.author: Roosterwiesel
posts.body:
I am very new to RPG Maker and also new to making sprites (I use Aseprite a bit, still learning).
I already made some graphics, but I have a problem now. My sprites are not all same size. Some are bigger, some smaller. They are also not 100% correct for RPG Maker MZ, only close.
Characters are fair easier for me imo
So my main question is:
Is it possible to use different sprite sizes in RPG Maker MZ?
Or do all sprites need to be exact same size always?
And if not possible:
Is there a way to fix different sizes without remaking everything?
Or what is best way/workflow to avoid this problem in future?
i actually was hoping to find a tutorial video exactly for this if I don*t plan to use the standard rpgmaker look and use more or less custom assets
Right now I feel a bit stuck because I don’t know if I can still use what I made

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
You’ll want to provide some screen shots of the sprite sheets you’re referring to. Visuals help a lot.
Others will be able to answer far better than myself, but yes I believe character sprites can be different sizes in RMMZ. I’ve never done it myself, but it was explained to me once that the engine will automatically calculate the dimensions of a character sprite sheet based on the overall canvass size. I would wait for someone else to respond, in case I got this wrong.
The only confident advice I ca provide is, for continuity, it’s best to ensure your pixel resolution is the same. Unless that is your deliberate intention, it will look odd if some sprites have larger pixels than others

posts.body:
cockwiesel said:

Click to expand...
Size doesn't really matter
At least that's what all the women have told me
Instead you must adhere to the formatting standards.
That is, 12 cells comprised of 3 columns and 4 rows.
The height and width of each cell can be of any resolution (within reason), so long as you have the 3x4 set up.
For a full sprite sheet (multiple characters like the default NPC character sheets), it's going to be 8 sets of these 12 cells, arranged in a 4x2 layout; or in other words: 12 columns by 8 rows.

If you want to change the tilesize instead of the spritesize, then you will need a plugin.
and since plugins can only affect the game, not the editor, you would need placeholder tilesheets in the editor's size (48x48) that are replaced by the true size tilesheets when ingame.
Shaz wrote such a plugin for RMMV, but I don't know opf any plugin for MZ that does the same.
and you'll need one that can be configured for your tilesize of 62x62

posts.author: KaijuuKimi
posts.body: You can create up to 128x128 tilesize with not much issue using Shaz tile size plugin. You might want to use 64 instead of 62 to make scaling easier as tile usually multiplication of 8.
